- Countrycode converts different country code formats

```{r}
library(sf)
library(tidyverse)
library(countrycode)
```

### Reading data

```{r}
hdr <- read_csv(list.files(pattern = "time_series", full.names = TRUE),
                locale = locale(encoding = "latin1"),
                na = " ")

world <- st_read(list.files(pattern = "\\.geojson$", full.names = TRUE))
```

notes:

- **`list.files(pattern = ...)`** finds the files by part of their name, so you don’t need to type the long names. Because your project folder is the working directory, it looks there automatically.

- **`read_csv()`** reads the CSV table. It’s not spatial data, so it’s not `st_read()`

- **`locale(encoding = "latin1")`** helps R read special characters in country names (like the ô in Côte d’Ivoire) without errors

- **`na = " "`** treats blank cells as missing values

#### Checking column names (good practice)

```{r}
names(world)
```

### Calculating difference 

```{r}
# first part
gii <- hdr %>%
  select(iso3, country, gii_2010, gii_2019) %>%
  mutate(gii_diff = gii_2019 - gii_2010)

# second part
world_gii <- world %>%
  mutate(iso3 = countrycode(ISO, origin = "iso2c", destination = "iso3c")) %>%
  left_join(gii, by = "iso3")
```

notes:

First part

- **`select()`** keeps only the columns you need: the 3-letter code, country name, and the GII scores for 2010 and 2019

- **`mutate(gii_diff = ...)`** creates the **new difference column** the task asks for

Second part

- **`countrycode` =** to join two tables, they need **matching columns**. The world file (world_gii) uses **two-letter (ISO)** codes while the HDR data uses **three-letter** codes (ISO3), so they don’t match.

  - **`countrycode(ISO, origin = "iso2c", destination = "iso3c")`** converts the two-letter codes into three-letter ones, in a new `iso3` column

  - **`left_join(gii, by = "iso3")`** joins the inequality data onto the world map, matching rows by `iso3`. “Left” means **keep every country in `world`**, even ones with no GII data (they’ll just get `NA`).

### Checking if it maps (good practice)

```{r}
plot(world_gii["gii_diff"])
```
